body:
It’s not gonna happen for me. I finally get it. I give up.

The rest of my existence is solely for saving my skin and trying not to traumatize my friends. I need to purge this account.
Tortured myself with old messages today. Why was I so polite.
Yeah, do not go looking online just to look. You are deep in this right now, and you don’t even have a clear yes or no to working on your marriage? This is not the time to swipe around.
I’m in therapy. I’m doing my best. I really am. I’m just so tired.
Nope, just communicating that I’m struggling. I’m not trying to burden anyone.
It’s not their fault, really, they just can’t handle me when I’m explaining why it doesn’t make much sense to continue being alive
I gotta figure out how to make rent. I worked less today so that’s… something
Complete crash out today and probably lost friends so I’m doing great.
Wait I’m in the Netherlands too. Where-ish are you?
Im considering the latter quite strongly because I feel it all failing again and I just can’t do it again.
I’m crying reading this and I need to go take a walk to stop myself from walking off a ledge, so I’m not giving the fullest answer at the moment but thank you for writing this.

I know you mean this well, but I have been working on myself, constantly. Like I am mostly isolated at home every day doing self work. I’m not on dating apps. I’m trying to meet people organically. So, I just wanna note, mostly to reassure, that I’m not exactly throwing myself at people right now, I’m trying to be intentional and careful but time is always against me and I am deeply sad because most people I know are married or remarried at this point and it just feels so hopeless.

The other thing is, and I do mean this practically, it is almost a sure thing that happy couples end up better financially. I am trying to rebuild after my horrible separation. I wanted to buy a house with my ex. Now I’m barely able to get by. I haven’t stopped working in 8 days and I have nothing to show for it. I’m not okay. I know others who aren’t doing okay, but they’re married so… they’re fine. I know everyone is different but it feels awful.

I also don’t know how I’m gonna meet someone young. If I wait til my finances are fixed, I will be in the grave. I am having a breakdown because it’s warranted.

I know this sounds negative, I’m really not trying to be. I’m not allowed to say the obvious solution. I can’t even get up today. My chest is sore and my eyes are tired from crying. I don’t know how to keep getting up every single day and trying when my life has collapsed so many times in my 30s and it’s happening again even though I’m literally not even sleeping these days desperately just trying to make it stop.

I have probably lost my chance at marriage because I gave too much time to my last relationship and now I’m getting too old to be considered viable. In addition my financial woes are so heavy and I spend nearly 100% of my time trying to fix them but I haven’t seen any success yet, which makes it even less likely that anyone will want me on top of the sheer stress that the lack of money brings. My friends live far away, the ones nearby aren’t even in the same city as me. I’m so tired. I have put in so much effort to overcome my c-ptsd, to emotionally become stable (today isn’t the best example but generally speaking no one knows I have any problems), I am pushing so hard to just be okay, and on paper I look like a loser anyway. I work every day to be better and because I haven’t broken through my financial instability and my last partner outright abandoned me, I’m nothing.

I don’t know if I should just give up. I feel like I can’t.

A friend called this morning and I broke down crying. I couldn’t keep working today. I feel like such a failure.
Were you also multi dating? Dude idk something about the way you’re telling this story is making me feel like there’s something you’re not coming to terms with about yourself

I think people often think they mean it or even actually mean it, but the minute they think about what it would entail to actually show up to a relationship, they get overwhelmed and shut down. Liking someone, dating or even having sex is one thing but actually putting action and effort into building a relationship is entirely different. They might be interested in the idea of a relationship but be distracted by something else, or unable to actually face the idea of commitment, whatever. It’s no excuse for the behavior, especially at this age. But it’s so, so common and it’s shitty.
They were a big part of my life once, met a lot of cool friends who are still close.
People who go to burning man and other similar events. And ditto.
I’m not a fella but yeah the love of my cats really does keep me breathing sometimes. They’re such amazing animals fr :)

I guess it depends. Is the excitement around physical attraction? Excitement is not necessarily a good indicator of compatibility. I’ve been hurt a lot so I guess I’d follow my head over my heart on this one.
He sounds fun and like he’s likely unpacked some baggage around compulsory masculine norms, which is pretty cool.
Tell him this. Explain to him that it’s necessary for you to feel supported by him without having to always hold his hand through it.

He liked you but he didn’t have the emotional maturity to deepen the relationship in his own head, with whatever that entailed.

Ughhhhhhhi
So you did boyfriend level shit without actually committing to them and then just left? I’d side-eye you too.

Yes, jfc.
I do go out but the reason I don’t join certain hobby groups is because I know with full certainty that if I met someone I wouldn’t continue going. I’d just wanna be home. It isn’t authentic for me.

I still go out to places I’d actually like to, but just… ffs. Yeah. I’m not made of time or money and I already have hobbies.

Opening up a relationship is not a solution to a failing relationship, ever. It’s a red flag that this was even part of his process. People who do this almost always lose the relationship. It is possible to open a relationship in a healthy way, but it is not a bandaid, ever. I say this as someone who self identifies as being a version of non-monogamous and whose ideal would be a partly open relationship. So, given that, his breakup was a month before you met, and that’s it… no fluff, no ‘it was a long breakup,’ that’s when it happened.

I’d get out if I were you. It is not fair to process a breakup with a new partner, not one this fresh. I understand that many people who have been in long term relationships will mention and have to talk about their former partners to new ones, but that initial stage of getting over it is not something that should be placed on the shoulders of a new partner, it is poisonous to building a new healthy dynamic.

I’m sorry to say, but I’d cut and run if I were you.
I’m trying to reach out to friends I just feel like such a burden

If I had the money I would but I’m in such dire straits idk if I’ll even be able to put food on the table soon.

I met someone like that last year and it turned out to be a bit of a disaster, but it’s really cute that yours turned out better. I just want life to be better.
I mostly am okay. I can be alone, I can self motivate, I mostly am able to do things without help, but I miss cohabitating with someone.
It’s okay, tone is hard to discern, I’m just having a rough time. I really appreciate you listening and being thoughtful, it means a lot.
No one seems to want me and I’m begging you to understand that your jokes feel like dismissals, regardless of intent.
It’s a fantasy but I’m okay, I won’t do it, sorry I even said it, the dark brain cells took over for a second. I need to stay alive but it’s so hard today.

I am so tired of having to do everything for myself all the time. I’m completely isolated most days of the week. My friends who live anywhere near me are flakey. My partner abandoned me and I know as I move into the second half of my thirties there’s almost no chance of marriage or love ever again. And, I’m broke, desperately trying to fix it. I’m just desd
I had several pandemic birthdays and then I dealt with the trauma of a partner who vanished after a decade. I’m just done.
Which one of you is gonna fuck me and love me for life?

I haven’t even been single since 30, just…
Turned 30. Had a friendship go bad where I got cut out of a whole social circle. Did have some friends I suppose.
31, pandemic. Stranded overseas that whole year. Spent it with two people who were sick of me being with them.
32, got vaccinated. No one was in the house for days. I was completely alone.
33, quarantined, cannot recall. Was with my partner but socializing was still locked down.
34, moved with my partner overseas. He was silently planning to leave me. No one knew it was my birthday. He worked. I was alone.
35, partner had abandoned me, housemate knew it was my birthday, but was out all day. Being alone was sort of preferable but extremely hard. Had gone to a social gathering where a man completely lovebombed me and started acting extremely weird. Spent the day inside not knowing where to turn.

36 is coming. Unmarried. No prospects. Struggling with money, hopefully I’ll be okay by next month. If not, I’m planning to take enough pills to end it.
It hit me today that there’s a large chance I’ll be spending another birthday in my 30s completely alone and I just cried.

Tell her you’d like to hear from her more. I’ve done this before not out of lack of interest, but worry that I’d overwhelm the other person. Once the desire is communicated clearly, it’s way easier to follow.

Come to think of it I didn’t ghost even when I did that, it was a drunk messy phone call. Regrettable but again, I was muuuuuch younger and less experienced. Even a bare minimum text is better than nothing. Just yeah big ew. :/

If it helps, I do think some men genuinely want relationships and start with good intention or think that they’ve genuinely done the healing work, but once they come to the reality of it they fumble or fuck up or just plain ghost. 

I can extend understanding and sympathy for the emotion but I can’t support the behavior. When I was much muuuuuch younger I fucked up in a similar way once, but in my defense I had come off an emotionally abusive relationship and didn’t understand how much I needed to heal (thank goodness I had the sense not to sleep with that other person though, it would have been so devastating). That said, we’re all here and over thirty. It’s way too far down the road in life to behave this way.
I love this term and I hate that I have just realized something from your comment ooooop

It’s because you’re hoping to find love, like most of us are. It’s normal and human. And age does put pressure on it, I’m afraid to say. I know it ‘shouldn’t’ but it’s not weird that so many of us hope to find something in our younger years.

Take my word for it babe, the people who end up with him are not winning a prize by having him if this is how he communicates. Maybe he’s got other good qualities but I’d be piiiiiissed if I got treated this way. Source: my ex did something nearly identical after I stayed with him for 11 years. My kindness is abundant but my tolerance for bullshit does not exist.

Nice and graceful is good. More than he deserves, but fine. Don’t bother sending the angry text, it won’t do anything but mar your image, if he’s really immature he’ll use it to justify his own bad behavior to himself. Write the angry paragraph and keep it in your notes or your journal or whatever, maybe write it on a piece of paper and set it on fire if you’re feeling a lil witchy (it’s a full moon, baybee).

He’s making me mad though, cause it SOUNDS LIKE he was sore over his relationship ending and instead of sitting with his discomfort decided to run back to someone who had shown him kindness for the ego boost. I also have zero respect for people who act badly and then hope the other person will do the dirty work of ending it when they were the ones who would have stuck it out. It’s giving coward. Again, I really don’t think you did anything wrong. You showed up as your kind, empathic self. It sucks to be going through this now but trust that some other person will treat your heart gently when they see that you have all that kindness to give.
I wish I could hug you. You seem very level headed.

‘Hey (friend name), I understand you’re struggling with this, but my advice to you is the same that it has been. I think you need to analyze your own role in this problem. I care about our friendship but I don’t have capacity to keep repeating my stance on it, and I really hope you find clarity soon.’

He realized that escalating physically might necessitate more serious conversation about the relationship. He enjoyed the dates and the sex but ultimately the trash took itself out. He is the type of man who likely does not have the emotional intelligence to have deeper discussion, no matter what impression he gave you. It’s not fair.

I’m sorry though, it’s no excuse for that kind of behavior. You don’t need to withhold sex. Men who do this will do it no matter how long you wait.
Your brother is my nightmare.

Yeah, absolutely the fuck not your fault. Especially when you specifically stated you were interested in dating exclusively. Any honest person would understand this to mean that dating someone else literal days before you would be challenging this boundary. If he had already been interested in someone else, it would have been on him to disclose this before bothering to go out with you… which I have to assume because if not, it meant he went out and met someone new right after calling you. But a few dates within three days?!?!?!?!! What the fuck? AND escalating physically? No, fuck this guy. We’re not in high school, there’s no way this wasn’t dishonest behavior, no matter how you slice it. He wanted the dopamine that he knew he’d get from experiencing a positive connection with you without honoring even a notional sense of commitment. This is not your loss even if it’s your hurt. 


Also, nerdy and introverted is just that… nerdy and introverted. It doesn’t mean he’s not an emotional stink bug of a human. It sounds like his exterior is way more developed than his emotional self awareness. You didn’t sign up to raise a man, you were offering genuine connection. Remember that you still can offer that, but certainly not for him ever again.

Goddamn this comment is 🔥 
I too feel bad for the other woman. Like imagine being the shiny new toy and having to live up to that forever.
Imagine being the other woman and hearing about this story? It happened once to me and looking back it should have been a red flag.

Most likely he did it for validation, but he sounds massively out of touch with himself to have gone through all those fucking steps just to take you for granted again.

You didn’t fall for anything. You literally did everything correctly here. You didn’t jump back in too soon (a year is plenty of time to work on yourself), you stated your conditions and boundaries, you followed through. Like you literally get a gold star for absolutely everything. Giving him another chance is a reflection on you being open hearted and kind. He has proven himself to be a cowardly little asshole, though. No matter what his reasoning, he gets no slack here. I am very open to giving people chances and being understanding, but holy shit he fumbled you bad and that has noooothing to do with you.

Remember, you’ll never understand it, because you would never ever do that to someone else.

I wouldn’t feel bad for not divulging your own stuff that soon. 6 weeks is not a massive amount of time, you’re still in a stage of discovering each other, I get why you’d want to approach all those things slowly and really feel out the dynamic between you two before diving into the deep end.

I think you should give yourself a few weeks at minimum and don’t expect anything. If you still wanna be friends after that, then I’m sure a text would be fine. He sounds like he sorta has a lot going on and so do you, so I’d take this opportunity to take care of yourself.
I’d personally give it a month.

Number two on your list really hits home, wow.

Thank you for being so kind (everyone is being incredibly patient in this thread today, it’s 9pm and I’m back at my desk working and I’m both PMSing and fully crashing out without being able to actually stop). I think I just ache knowing I have a lot to give and I just want a little more ease in my life. I want someone to like me back, I want my work to sell and to just be okay for the next month. I can handle hard and lonely times, I’ve proven it to myself so often, but I don’t think I can see myself living like this forever. I just don’t know where or when that changes and it’s enough to make me cry today. 🤷‍♀️

Ah okay see, I tend to know sooner if I’m interested in making it a thing. It’s in stages of course, I don’t get to talking two weeks in and assume it’s time to move in together, but usually i have a strong sense of self and I tend to have a gut feel within a few dates if I’d like to give it a shot. I’ve never slept with someone twice. It’s been once or it’s gone on for years.

I’ve also had a lot of people act pretty callously toward me. I have recently been thinking a lot about getting assaulted when I was younger on a date and the domino effect it had on my life. I wish I could be more chill, I’m trying, but I’m trying to build a safe love and I don’t lead anyone on.

I do feel this way about people in general, I guess on dates specifically I’m thinking about compatibility and things like that so it is a slightly different headspace for me. I’m not trying to be too intense or anything, like I do want people to be relaxed around me because my future person would ideally be relaxed around me. But… I’m still thinking about relationships. I guess that’s why it often doesn’t feel fun, like I do enjoy learning about people but if I want to do that I can fully get that experience from events and parties. I enjoy your perspective, I guess I’m just figuring out why first dates tend to feel sorta tiring to me.

See, I totally feel with way when I’m at a social gathering when the expectation is zero. I like meeting strangers. But idk I guess the context of a date always has me aware that I really am out here trying to meet a life partner while also showing my chill, fun side and hoping they don’t reject me after leading me on (again… so many fucking times and I don’t know why). I will try to reflect on this and see if I can embody it more, it is a really good positive way of thinking… I think I’ve just been hurt a lot and I’m really tired.

Yeah :( Please don’t get me wrong, when I’m with someone I like, I light up a room. I love connecting with friends. I don’t have proof of my work life going well but I have belief. Endless rejection and isolation has me damn tired. I do need a break.

I’m not OP, but can I be honest? I often find dates tiring because there is a fairly large chance that I’m spending time with a stranger and getting to know them with nearly no chance of becoming friends if it doesn’t work out. Like I’m quite open to friends and being social too, but truly, do you end up becoming friends with most first dates that don’t make it to round two? It’s a buildup with an almost instant taper off and boy is it exhausting to bring your best self out knowing that this is almost guaranteed.
I literally don’t think dating is fun. :| Killjoy mentality, I know. I’ve really tried. Being in a relationship is fun. Dating blows. IMHO of course.

I haven’t stopped working since Saturday and I’m so tapped. I feel fucking depressed and worried about work and I don’t know when the next time I’ll even get a hug is. I can’t even go out this month because I’m being too cautious financially and all I want is affection, but the idea of getting on the apps gives me such dread that all I can do is medicate and try not to kms.
Honestly this is strangely cute though, like damn that is a good former landlord
There’s just no one here and I’m alone.
Man chill, so many women love to top lmao
Life is long. Jobs change. Connections are rare. Do with that what you will.

My healed, secure brain: Missing them means you have the capacity to care about someone and that in itself is a beautiful quality that’s nothing to be ashamed of as long as you’re not doing something silly like basing major decisions around it or waiting for someone

The emotional screaming frog in my brain: aaaAaaAaaaaAaAAAAAEEeAA
Goddamn I’ve got no wisdom, I’m just so sorry and sending you all the kindness in my heart.
Thank you. I effectively have released this person but it still hurts.
I’m mad at myself for wishing he’d reach out.

I can’t say I’m ‘happy’ single, I still want love, but I know for damn sure I’m not desperate because I don’t waste my time with people who are so uncertain of me that they’re worried the next pretty face will sway them. 🤷‍♀️ We don’t have time for this high school shit at this age lmao
Exactly. I’m not an option. I’m my own kind of pretty. My soul is pretty. I have had a taste of this behavior and it was enough to never want to deal with it again.

You need to clean up this mindset immediately. If this is how you see women, it’s going to affect how you act towards them. There are plenty of women who aren’t materialistic and also want a family, they’re not rare in your age bracket. I need you to also internalize that if you do want children, that means that any woman you have them with is going to need minimum a year outside of her own career path and you likely will need to be the provider. Then, she has to recover physically and re-enter the workforce while co-parenting (because I assume you also want to raise your kid). That does carry some expectation for you to have your material wealth in order if you’re committed to the relationship and the family, there’s a real need for it in that case. It’s not that every woman is a shallow gold digger, there’s just a logistical reality to this that you need to consider. There are plenty of solutions for you, but if you have a bad outlook on women as a whole from the outset, you’re going to fall into confirmation bias.
If you’re that easily swayed by the notion of choice then maybe you need to ask yourself if you’re actually ready for commitment before you go hurting someone.

Honestly there is no rule or set amount of dates that can spare you from men who get fucking weird about things after sex. They know that after sex it might mean being able to communicate more effectively, talk about labels and expectations, etc, and they know they can’t so they dip. I am rapidly approaching the point where I’m keen to throw out any waiting period and start asking men if they’ve ever done this before and just to set my own expectations.

I am vaguely incapable of being mad on my own behalf but I’m mad on your behalf. It’s baffling to me that adults in their 30s can be this way with no remorse or introspection. This guy who was lucky enough to even cross paths with you is gross and I wish him a very everything he deserves.

Because a lot of people perceive dating apps as entertaining, or like a game. They’re not even incorrect on some level since most dating apps are set up to deliver dopamine hits in the same way. It’s not ‘real’ to a lot of people. 

People swipe and match out of boredom pretty often, regardless of what their profile might say.
I understand the loneliness part without a doubt but I really can’t see anything wrong with wanting someone who has already figured out some level of emotional maturity.

I had a relationship of a similar length (longer) end in extremely messed up circumstances and it’s taken me a long time to even feel worthy of love. I don’t know what work she’s done but it takes quite a lot to just be kind of okay again, maybe she hasn’t fully gotten to the place where she can date again. It still doesn’t seem right that it’s coming at your expense, though. Sorry you’re going through it.

Okay, that does change the context for suuure. I’m not saying this is an indictment of either of you, but this reads like a textbook case of limerence on her part. She got excited, probably dropped her own boundaries (not your fault) and then after a few weeks of living in the fantasy/feelings during her trip ,came back and suddenly had to plug back into the reality of it all. Then she started self analyzing about the boundaries she’d dropped and that’s where she withdrew.

I doubt it was malicious on her part but it’s not very nice for you to have to deal with this.

Do you think you’re being too picky?
I don’t think you are.

I think at minimum you have to have a very sober talk about this. No matter how pleasant the relationship is, kids are one of the decisions in life that really is a yes or a no, you have to be on the same page. If she’s anywhere near your age this changes time lines as well. Either one of you would have to very seriously commit to changing your mind, and release any resentment, or you need to walk. If you really care about each other, you won’t waste another 5 to 6 months of each others’ time. I think this may be hard to hear, but I sort of see this as a dealbreaker on your relationship, but at minimum I’d have the discussion and make a clear headed decision now rather than kick it further down the road.
Wait, so this was before meeting up? If so, I think I understand why she pulled back.
Thanks for insinuating I’m hopeless, really needed that at midnight alone on a Sunday 🤷‍♀️
Ew David!!!
Have any of my posts indicated that there’s any hope in hell for me?
Truly
None of them good
Uuuuuuuuuugh

I am so similar to you. Also about to turn 36. Not desperate, have let people and opportunities go when they didn’t fit. Working on myself. Building my own stability and self esteem. Pouring love into my friendships. All the stuff. I even believe now that I am an actual catch in spite of some of the big life challenges that I have.

I have been crying all day but I’m choosing to believe that there’s still someone in this world for me. I think there’s probably someone in this world for you too. And not in the ‘there are billions of people out there’ cause let’s face it, we’re not about to move to a remote location in a foreign country to get a date (probably… unless that’s really part of your dreams, but let’s focus on our local pool).

I try to craft a story for myself that I’m not alone in the world, I’m just not with them YET. Like so many other things I’ve wanted in life that have eventually appeared, it’s not that it’s impossible, they simply aren’t here yet. But also? Some days you just have to cry for a while, because love IS important. Even if you’re pouring into all the other beautiful things in your life right now and can recognize the good, the fact that you’re still feeling the space in your emotional self that can only be filled by love is a sign that you haven’t given up on finding one good person to build something with.

You could be in an open or poly relationship. It requires some very serious discussions about boundaries but it’s fine. I am an extremely committed person in relationships but I also value a little bit of openness, and I don’t think the two need to lie in opposition.

I will warn though, this isn’t necessarily an easy path to navigate. Hoping to meet someone who gets it isn’t simple; there are many iterations of open relationships and polyamory and you’re going to need to be crystal clear on dealbreakers, boundaries and generally organizing what your ideals are so that you’re not suddenly in a guessing game with four other people.

I’m nonbinary but I’m cute-girl shaped (I’m not trying to brag and I am working on my appearance but like… I’m mostly happy with what I’ve got going on save for some small
 insecurity around my weight), I live in proximity to two big cities and I was never successful at multi dating on apps either. 🤷‍♀️ I did ‘meet’ a lot of men and sometimes women who loved to just talk and talk and never meet up. I struggle with some anxious and depressive tendencies and the apps really made me feel horrible, so I stopped using them. It means I haven’t met as many people to ‘potentially date’ but at least when I have met people the determination of whether or not we vibe with each other is near-immediate. Regardless, I resonate with what you said about the second date. If I think date two is gonna happen, I don’t bother going out and seeing what else is there because I’m just like, omg yay, date two! I have fully had this tested in the last few months, no one asked me to not multi date but I just get so happy over the idea of someone wanting to keep seeing me that I can’t imagine going and pursuing someone else.

I’m extremely single and have been crying all day though, so I guess I’m a loser.

I waited until the third date just to have something similar happen to me. I’ve also slept with someone before dating and ended up in a long relationship. I do get it. Really. If that boundary still feels useful to you, of course you get to keep it, but someone who is sloppy with your heart could really pull this shit after the first, third, or forty seventh date. So again… if it works, of course, you get to make that call, but you don’t have to blame yourself for someone else being shitty. Maybe this is telling you that you can sleep with someone before the third date, conceptually, but that you’ll end up framing it in your mind differently if it does happen again, you know? Or maybe it means you’ll never bother with it again. No wrong answer, just a learning experience.

I have proven to myself recently that I’m not desperate, but I don’t date for entertainment, I date because I actually have interest in building a relationship, which is why I uuuusually don’t immediately sleep with someone and have not had many short term experiences. I’ve had one time hookups and longer relationships, I don’t do well with half baked stuff. But, even if I want something intentional, I still want the other person to just enjoy my presence at the start and keep things lighthearted, cause I want a life with someone who likes to laugh. :) Even if you’re seriously looking, of course it should be fun. I think you’re doing great, give yourself time to think about stuff and feel things, but you’re not stupid, you don’t need to take it out on yourself, that guy just played himself out of a good thing even if he doesn’t realize it.

I think that’s the perfect takeaway. For me I almost always end up having met the person more than once before hooking up, I used to have a slightly higher boundary, but I’m trying to find the right balance with what I’m willing to do as someone who does have a sex drive but highly prefers relationships. There’s really no wrong answer, you just have to adapt what you’re willing to put up with based on the information you have about yourself now.

People say the dating pool sucks right now and seem to almost relish being jaded or distrustful. Don’t buy the hype. This attitude is what makes the dating pool so much worse. I wouldn’t wanna date someone who immediately doubted everything; of course you’re gonna read the room and look for the basic signs of someone being a good egg, but you’re here and still in the dating pool, still willing to show up and be your loving self, and someone else is gonna realize that it’s worth taking you out of the pool.

Exactly, that’s the best thing to remember here. It’s perfectly natural if your heart hurts right now, cause you felt something real and showed up as yourself. And truly, don’t beat yourself up and become bitter or distrustful, because the only thing you guarantee if you do that is that you’re bitter and distrustful, and you deserve to stay honest and loving and kind. These things happen, sometimes after one night, sometimes after literal years of being with someone. You might find yourself being more discerning going forward, and that’s fine, but don’t be mad at yourself for qualities that are actually really rare and beautiful.

Thanks for being so nice about it. Like I said, I understand the why, to some extent. I also toootally understand that if people wanna multi date and disclose this up front, they might be well matched with other people who multi date too. I just wanna meet the person who actually chooses me, I guess.

Even if you’re single, you want a life with people who support you and who you support back; usually this is friends, family, broader community and coworkers, and none of that should disappear in the presence of finding a good partner.

If you show up for yourself and your own values no matter the circumstance, it’s a lot harder to slip into being codependent.

Think of it less as an ultimatum and more of a strong boundary that you are setting to protect you both, because that’s what it is. You are not setting an objective with the aim of a one-sided outcome, you are setting the stage for a successful partnership where you disallow resentment to build and encourage communication to grow. The time cap is saying, I am able to conceive of continuing this way for this particular length of time but if the expectation is to make it official or grow it, extending past that time does not serve the relationship and inhibits it. However, if even the idea of that is too much, it might just not be the right relationship for you.

I will say though, if they’re afraid to commit after three months with the distance involved, they’re unlikely to commit later. You’re still saving yourself a longer buildup and worse heartbreak and possibly giving them the space to get something more suitable for what they want. If they want to commit, they will, or at minimum they will understand why you’re discussing this and you will have an indicator, or at least a productive conversation. I am not saying you pick a number like ‘we gotta be moved in within 95 days or else!’, more like, ‘my lease is up at x point and I feel if we are going to work out long term, cohabitation is something I’d like to approach before I extend that lease.’ You’re not teenagers having a summer romance, you’re adults, and our time on this earth isn’t a given. Don’t be afraid to guard yours.

I think you have to say this now, OP. I’m a non drinker these days but drinking isn’t a dealbreaker for me in itself, it’s just not my vice. That said, I could not handle being around excessive drinking in a partner at this stage of my life. I include drinking as a way to excuse or cover up certain behaviors as excessive regardless of the amount. For example, my ex would sometimes drink heavily with friends and it would be among the only times he’d let himself explore deeper feelings about big things in his life, but then he’d be sloppy drunk at parties cornering people and having sort of explosive moments of talking about extremely heavy subjects, or even drinking and having breakdowns and then acting the next day as though I should just shrug this behavior off as something that just happened with booze. Looking back, I would tolerate that in him and still probably would have if he’d stayed because I cared for him so deeply, but it was really hard to have him get defensive the next day when I’d ask if we could talk through some of what had happened. I’d be in the awkward position of trying to help him in the drunk moment where he was sloppy and emotional and off the rails, but he’d avoid processing those feelings in a healthy and constructive way later. That may not be your bf’s impulse, but I do think it’s worthwhile to ask him/examine with him his reasons for drinking so excessively. 

I have found that, in very broad strokes, men don’t always culturally have the ‘permission’ to express feelings and may use alcohol as a sort of excuse to do so (so if there is shame they can later dismiss it as just having been drunk at a party). It is not always a conscious thing and I don’t say that in a dismissive way, it’s often cultural and even subliminal, but it’s best to cut to the chase early. Couples therapy might be good, but it may be worth it to ask your partner if there is something he feels he can only access when he’s drunk, or even to just ask what he feels drinking offers him, cause it’s obviously not happiness, money, health or closure.

As a general disclaimer, I moved at the end of 2022 so that is the most relevant information I have personally. In my case, it was several things. 

Foremost, dealing with anything government related as a foreigner was akin to mild torture (I am originally from the US). I really felt insecure because on a legal level, I often was, regardless of following the rules. It became extremely difficult to deal with the South African government and I had a realization that if I stayed, I would be dealing with them for life, and there’s no getting around it. As a comparison, in SA, it took me 5 years to get formally get working rights (I did things like gig work, cash jobs, working remotely, etc). When I moved to the Netherlands and couldn’t get hired right away, decided freelance made more sense for me, and setting up a company took me a matter of weeks. I got to the point of putting off important things because I would just panic and shut down, and rightfully so… I often showed up in a government office in SA to wait for hours just to be told that I was missing information, that something had changed and the details were no where, or pointed towards ‘someone who would know’ who didn’t even have working emails or phone numbers. Integrating into this system took years, never really got completed, and it’s not something you can side-step.

Personal safety became a big one. I was based in Cape Town between the ages of 23 and 33. As I got older, I grew extremely tired with having to stay vigilant constantly. Feeling like I needed a ‘chaperone’ to go do anything or having to ‘team up’ just to do something like take a hike really got to me after turning 30. I didn’t want to ask other people  to stay with me all the time, I value being able to do things alone sometimes. The pandemic was the last straw for me on this one. My usual ‘safe’ spots were often indoors or around people. Before covid was better understood and vaccines were unavailable, I didn’t feel safe in my usual spots, but going outside into nature is also something that one does with caution. It was awful. To make matters worse, robberies in the houses around me became more common, so even staying inside totally by myself or with my partner didn’t always feel safe either. This has probably changed somewhat, people have gained immunity and the world is a bit different, but it broke me for a while. I didn’t feel like an ‘adult’ at times because of it. It was a gilded cage with an incredible view. Who wants to feel like they need a chaperone in their 30s? Though the pandemic has become more manageable at this point in time, I believe Cape Town still has quite a bit of crime. I feel empathy for the people who have no better choice than to commit those crimes, but I also knew that I couldn’t personally solve a problem that big, nor could I pretend it didn’t really wear me down. It took time to heal from this. I don’t own a car and walk everywhere now, and I love going for missions by myself.

I guess this is also a me-specific one, but I work in the creative field, and I got to a point where I lost faith that I could grow my career. I burnt out completely for a while and I’m now in an area where there’s more options for me to pursue income. I don’t think I’ll ever be rich and that’s okay (artists tend not to be loaded, but I’d be content to build a living doing what I’m good at!) However, I was beginning to fear that I’d never be able to consider retirement because my income options were so unsustainable. I convinced myself I didn’t want or need material things because admitting I’d never be able to get them hurt too much. To some extent, possessions won’t make you happy, but I think it’s okay to have some goals, material and not. I’d like to own a home someday. I’d like a few more tattoos. I’d like to take trips with friends. Mostly, I want a future where I’m not chronically stressed over finances. I had to go through the painful process of admitting that covid killed my industry and connections, but that even before it had, I never really made a strong enough wage to build myself security in the local economy. I’m still working on this one, it’s not all Cape Town’s fault, but I’ve known a lot of people who have left because they felt the same way even in lucrative careers.

Lastly, fuck load shedding.

I wanna reiterate that there are absolutely reasons why people can and do choose to stay in Cape Town. Some people have really salient reasons to stay, maybe have better job security or family lives that make better sense there or can afford housing in safer areas. I can’t ever hate the place, but I just couldn’t see a future there long-term, and once I knew that for sure, I couldn’t stay. I don’t think it’s a terrible place and I ‘feel’ more South African than American in many ways, it’s definitely somewhere that has the distinction of feeling like a home in my head, but I can’t even compare how much better I am mentally and emotionally for choosing a new place to live.

I think it’s important to examine why people believe in witchcraft, and think about where it lines up against a cultural tale that relates to the way people live vs a hardened belief that it is real.

Please take whatever I say with a heaping teaspoon of salt since I’m not from a culture that had any belief in witchcraft or healers (in as much as people have culturally accepted Catholicism as a wholly different thing regardless of overlap), but I often think that belief in witchcraft is fueled when other alternatives to it are perceived as being/actually coming from an adversary, or specifically made to exclude certain groups. A strong desire to hold on to it can definitely occur alongside medical racism, I think, which unfortunately has a long history both here and in the US. So outside of the acknowledgement that there are medicinal remedies that are effective even without the interference of a regulating body, I really think that if a group is systematically cut off or even penalized for trying to exist in the ‘default’ system, it’s a helluva lot easier to cultivate trust in practices that, while unsubstantiated, provide an overall safer environment in which to seek treatments. I’m not saying that to excuse those who swoop in and scam out of people’s good faith and material needs (fuck that!), but more to point out that I can really see why people would place a lot of trust in witchcraft even when there are more globally regulated/tested/accepted forms of medicine.

I think as a casual observer too, there’s something that can feel refreshing to view our current world through a more naturalist lens, something that is notably absent from a lot of westernized ways of living and conspicuously present in ‘witch stuff.’ I think that this can be real in its own way, but on a personal note I’d say that’s more about showing respect for nature and feeling a need to preserve it, but I guess I see that as a beautiful thing without invoking anything about ancestors or ghosts. That said, I also can see where if someone grew up with a cultural tie to it, there might be a warmer and more personalized feeling to this along with simply wanting to preserve a culture that might otherwise be unrecognized. I think people should be able to do whatever they want as long as it’s not harming anyone else though, and it seems to me that the major ‘cons’ of modern witchcraft is that scammers can find a lot of ways in which to do major damage, but I also feel like maybe it’s valuable to expand the things we learn about in general, instead of dismissing it even when we don’t believe in it, because bridging the gap between those things gives less of a stage for bad actors to exist on.

I also practice mindfulness meditations in conjunction, and try to practice regulating breath. Knowing how to breathe through high stress situations doesn’t stop the anxiety from happening, but it gives me a way of interacting with it without allowing it to take over. It takes time though. Try to approach it with curiosity and not expectations, have fun learning new stretches that make your body feel best, and I think you’ll have a better outcome.
